title: Topology
subtitle: A free-move map of your server estate — drag to arrange, scroll to zoom.

empty.title: No servers mapped yet
empty.description: Once you add hosts, VMs, containers and their relationships, your estate will appear here as a draggable diagram.

error.title: Couldn't load the topology
error.description: The infra map failed to load. Try again in a moment.

agent.outdatedTooltip: This agent ({agentVersion}) is a major version behind your server ({serverVersion}). Update the agent binary to stay compatible.
agent.policyAppliedTooltip: This host is running the current fleet agent policy (v{revision}).
agent.policyPendingTooltip: This host is still running policy v{revision}; the current one is v{current}. It picks the new one up on its next check-in and applies it from the run after that.

pending.title: Pending review
pending.description: Hosts the reporting agent discovered. Confirm to add them to your inventory, or discard.
pending.searchPlaceholder: Search name or IP (srv-* works too)
pending.noMatches: No pending items match these filters.
pending.selectedCount: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing selected} one {# selected} other {# selected}}
pending.hostAlreadyReviewed: This server has already been reviewed.
pending.overCap: {count} selected — one bulk action takes at most {max}. Narrow the selection (a filter helps) and run it in more than one pass.

merge.title: Merge {label} into another server
merge.description: Use this when this host is one you already have — a server that was re-imaged and came back with a new machine ID, or a clone that was separated out. The reporting key moves to the server you pick, so it keeps receiving reports; this row is archived.
merge.suggestionsDescription: These servers report the same hardware serial or network card address as this one. A suggestion, not a decision — pick one only if you know that box was re-imaged.
merge.targetDescription: The server you pick keeps its own name, kind, position, owner and asset link. Everything the agent owns moves onto it with the reporting key: the reported hardware and software facts, the status, the last check-in and the agent version — and the IP too, unless that IP was set by hand. If it already reports through an agent of its own, that key is replaced: a host still checking in with it will come back as a new pending server.

confirm.title: Confirm this server
confirm.description: Add this agent-discovered host to your live topology. You can re-classify or rename it first.
confirm.trackAsAssetDescription: On by default — also create a tracked Asset (with the reported host facts) so this server can carry an owner, KB links and secrets. Turn off to keep it graph-only.

onboarding.title: Track servers automatically
onboarding.description: Install a lightweight agent on a Linux server and it reports its hardware & software to lazyit by itself — it can only report, nothing else.
onboarding.noPermissionHint: Ask an administrator to add a reporting agent — it needs the manage-settings permission.

wizard.title: Create a reporting agent
wizard.subtitle: Install a reporting agent on a Linux server in three steps.
wizard.whatIsAgent: An agent is a tiny program you run on a server. It reports the server's hardware and installed software to lazyit by itself — it can't read or change anything else.
wizard.nameHint: A name to recognise this agent later (for example the server's name).
wizard.scopeNote: This token can only report inventory (infra:report). It can't read or change anything else, and every host it reports lands in Pending review for your approval.
wizard.requirements: You'll run this on a Linux server with root access.
wizard.installHint: Copy the command and run it on the Linux server as root. The token is shown only once — capture it before closing.

manual.step2: Make it executable and move it into place:

wizard.waitDescription: Run the install command on your server. As soon as the agent checks in, it'll show up here — usually within a couple of minutes.
wizard.successDescription: Your server checked in. Confirm it to add it to your inventory.

servers.title: Servers
servers.subtitle: Every node in your topology — filter, search and open one to see its owner, secrets and connections.

create.title: Add a node to the map
create.description: Map a host, VM, container or any other part of your estate.
create.trackAsAssetDescription: On by default — the node gets a backing asset so it can carry an owner, KB links and secrets. Turn off for ephemeral nodes like containers.
create.linkAssetSearch: Search by name, tag or serial…
create.linkAssetDescription: Leave empty to create a minimal asset named after the node.

panel.noOwners: No owner — this node isn't tracked as an asset, or no one is assigned.
panel.noSecrets: No secret references. Values are never shown here — only handles.
panel.secretHandleNote: Reference only — the value is never revealed here.
panel.secretPickerEmpty: No secrets found. You only see secrets you can access.
panel.noChildren: Nothing runs on this node yet.
panel.statusDescription: Set the node's live state. The reporting agent will drive this automatically later.
panel.ipConflictWarning: {count, plural, one {This IP is also used by # other node} other {This IP is also used by # other nodes}}
panel.shortcutInvalid: Each shortcut needs a label and a valid URL.
panel.impactDescription: If this node goes down, what stops with it? Highlights the downstream nodes on the map.
panel.impactSafe: Nothing depends on this node — safe to take down.
panel.impactCount: {count, plural, one {# node affected if this goes down} other {# nodes affected if this goes down}}

delete.title: Remove this node from the map?
delete.descriptionSuffix: off the map. Its history is kept and it can be restored later.

edges.title: Connections
edges.description: How this node relates to the rest of your estate.
edges.addDescription: Pick the relationship and the other node.
edges.directionNote: This node is the source; the relationship points to the other node.

bulk.confirmDescription: Each item is confirmed exactly as it would be one at a time: {hosts, plural, one {# server} other {# servers}} and {containers, plural, =0 {no containers} one {# container} other {# containers}}. You are still approving every one of them.
bulk.trackHostsLabel: Track the {count, plural, one {server} other {# servers}} as inventory assets
bulk.trackHostsDescription: On by default, as for a single confirm — a server is a thing you own, assign and warranty, so it gets an Asset carrying the reported host facts.
bulk.trackContainersLabel: Track the {count, plural, one {container} other {# containers}} as inventory assets
bulk.trackContainersDescription: Off by default. A container is replaced by the next deploy, has no serial to record, and one Docker host can add dozens — so they stay on the map without adding Assets nobody will curate. Turn it on if a container really is something you track.
bulk.kindDescription: Leave this alone unless the agent got the classification wrong for the whole selection.
bulk.discardDescription: This takes them off the map. Their history is kept and they can be restored later — the same as discarding one at a time. If the agent reports them again they will come back as new pending items.
bulk.appliedToast: {count, plural, one {# item done} other {# items done}}.

rules.title: Auto-confirm rules
rules.description: Write down a judgement once instead of repeating it for every discovered host. A rule you wrote is still your decision — you can disable or delete it at any time, and every server it confirms is recorded against your name.
rules.notRetroactive: A rule only applies to reports that arrive after you save it. Nothing already waiting in this tray will be confirmed behind you — those are still yours to review.
rules.empty: No rules yet. Every discovered host waits here until you confirm it.
rules.namePlaceholder: Production servers on the management VLAN
rules.hostnameDescription: Use * for any run of characters and ? for exactly one — srv-* matches srv-app-04. The whole name has to match, not just part of it. A pattern of nothing but wildcards isn't a condition: it matches every host there is.
rules.subnetDescription: A CIDR block, IPv4 or IPv6. A host that reported no address never matches this. 0.0.0.0/0 isn't a condition either — it's every address there is.
rules.reportedKindDescription: What the agent's report made lazyit propose for this host — not what you want it to become.
rules.trackAsAssetDescription: On by default for a servers-only rule, off for any rule that can also match containers — the same reasoning as confirming by hand. Turn it on if these containers really are things you track.
rules.needsCondition: A rule needs at least one condition that can rule a host out: a name pattern with something other than * and ?, a subnet narrower than 0.0.0.0/0, or a reported kind. A condition that matches everything would confirm everything the agent finds.
rules.savedToast: Rule saved. It applies from the next report onwards.
rules.deletedToast: Rule deleted. Servers it already confirmed are unchanged.
rules.author: Written by {name}
rules.authorUnknown: Author no longer in the directory
rules.lastMatched: {count, plural, one {Used # time} other {Used # times}}, last on {when}
